hypotheses.name: cs25_thm2_band_to_list_bridge
hypotheses.statement: CS25 Theorem 2 (ePrint 2025/2046): if eps_ca(RS[F,D,k],delta) < (q-n)/(2kq) then |Lambda(RS[F,D,k+1],delta)| <= 2*eps_ca*q. Hence any target-2 closure proving eps_ca <= B*/(2q) at the official rate-1/2 row (which automatically satisfies eps < (q-n)/(2kq) since B*/q ~ 2^-128 << 2^-21 at KoalaBear k=2^20) discharges the ordinary-list budget |Lambda| <= B* at the same radius for the k+1 code — i.e., the MCA lane mechanically feeds target 1 at the k+1 row offset. Falsified if the k -> k+1 offset breaks official-row admissibility or the domain-D hypotheses exclude smooth cosets.

hypotheses.name: kkh_subset_sum_centers_feed_generator_economy
hypotheses.statement: The KKH/Kambire bad-scalar construction — r-fold sums of distinct elements of the order-2^alpha subgroup H, |H^{+r}| >= (s/2r)^r, on the two-monomial line X^{rm} + lambda*X^{(r-1)m} — instantiates target 10: at official rows the subset-sum family supplies >= B*/2^33 pairwise-distinct half-size subset-sum centers whose pairwise differences factor as height-budget units times elements of the small multiplicative semigroup generated by H. Falsified if the distinctness count falls short at v_2(q-1) >= 41 rows with q up to 2^256, or the height/semigroup factorization of differences fails, or their lemma structurally requires p polynomial in n.

hypotheses.name: lenstra_antipodal_char0_closure_refinement
hypotheses.statement: Refinement of the seeded odd-weight parity hypothesis (not a duplicate): Lenstra Thm 2.2 with n = 512L, m = 2 forces every integer-coefficient vanishing sum of 512L-th roots to decompose into antipodal pairs zeta^j(1-1); since reduced slot configurations have distinct exponents in [0,256L) (no antipodal pairs available after folding -zeta^j = zeta^{j+256L}), ALL TEN slots — even-weight included, strictly beyond parity — are empty over characteristic zero. The entire live content of targets 14-23 is therefore the mod-q layer, where the toy relation 1 + zeta + zeta^3 = 0 in F_9 (zeta = 1+i, exact order 8) proves parity does not survive reduction and DZ02's CJ-type inequality is vacuous at 2-power reduced exponents; slot emptiness must be proved as 'no admissible prime q (v_2(q-1) >= 41, q < 2^256, plus the 2^32-deep AP condition) divides Norm_{Q(zeta_512L)/Q}(P(zeta))'. Falsified/decided by the pre-registered L=1 norm-factorization falsifier (hunt prime divisors ≡ 1 mod 2^41 among slot norms).

hypotheses.name: cdk_weight16_classification_covers_slot_subrelations
hypotheses.statement: The Christie-Dykema-Klep classification of minimal vanishing sums of weight <= 16 (arXiv:2008.11268) contains, after signed-to-unsigned folding, every possible characteristic-zero minimal subrelation of any slot configuration (w <= 11 < 16), and its explicit list confirms no minimal relation carries a reduced exponent of 2-adic valuation >= 9 — yielding an independent citable second proof of the char-0 slot closure and a certificate-generation template for target 11's ternary-kernel lattices. Falsified if their classification excludes signed configurations, imposes order normalizations incompatible with exact order 512L, or is only conjectural above weight 12.

hypotheses.name: stepanov_rigidity_feeds_spread_and_norm_gates
hypotheses.statement: The 2025-26 Stepanov/Hanson-Petridis rigidity wave — Kalmynin (mu_d = A+B forces |A| = |B|; A-A = mu_d ∪ {0} forces d in {2,6}), Kim-Yip-Yoo ((G-1)\{0} multiplicatively irreducible), Cochrane (a subgroup is a GAP iff |A_k| in {2,4,p-1}) — supplies pointwise |H ∩ (H+t)| and anti-structure bounds strong enough to (i) derive P-B's post-strip slope-spread anti-concentration at low core (target 4) and (ii) bound norm-gate coincidence counts (target 7) at the official rows. Falsified if the methods yield only qualitative statements (no explicit constants), degrade at d = 2^s, or require subgroup sizes outside the n^2 <= p <= 6^(n/4) window.

hypotheses.name: chen_zhang_line_ball_lemma_scoops_collinearity_floor
hypotheses.statement: The line/Hamming-ball intersection lemma in Chen-Zhang (STOC 2025, arXiv:2408.15925) — a line meets a ball of radius (s/(s+1))*Delta in at most s points — at s = 2 implies our headliner E (no three collinear list members at agreement a when n-K+1 > floor(3(n-a)/2)); headliner E must be repositioned as a citation/corollary in any writeup, not a novelty claim. Falsified only if exact statement comparison shows E covers a strictly larger radius/agreement range or a genuinely different object (list members vs arbitrary line points in a ball).

hypotheses.name: agl_alphabet_floor_locates_rate_half_crossing
hypotheses.statement: AGL23/BDG24 (arXiv:2308.13424; ABF Thm 3.10): achieving list ell at radius (ell/(ell+1))(1-rho-eta) requires alphabet size >= 2^{alpha_{ell,rho}/eta}; with q < 2^256 this floors eta >= alpha_{3,1/2}/256 at ell = 3, so at n = 2^41 the exact 3n/4 generalized-Singleton point is provably unattainable with list <= 3 and target 1's crossing a_L must sit at least eta*n = (alpha_{3,1/2}/256)*2^41 agreement units below it — quantitatively legitimizing the B*=3 four-codeword obstruction and bracketing the crossing. Falsified by extracting the explicit alpha_{3,1/2} and finding the implied bracket inconsistent with our exact four-adjacent-pair crossing replays (headliner F).
